name: Coastal Conservancy grants
summary: California state grants, awarded through a rolling pre-application, for projects that restore and protect the coast and coastal watersheds, expand public access and build climate resilience. Nonprofits and public agencies can apply.

geography.label: California coast, San Francisco Bay and coastal watersheds

eligibility.rule: Project is consistent with the funding source's purposes
Project is consistent with Conservancy enabling legislation
Can administer funds and deliver the project to state requirements, or has a fiscal sponsor for administrative support
Grantee has or will have the legal right to carry out the project
Grantee has a long-term management, maintenance and monitoring plan
Community groups without 501(c)(3) status and non-federally recognised tribes have a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor
Grant does not pay for operation or maintenance

status.quote: Most Conservancy grants are awarded through a rolling pre-application solicitation.

applicant_types.quote: Public Agencies, including Joint Power Authorities and Federally-Recognized Indian Tribes Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status Other community-based organizations and non-federally-recognized tribes may apply with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor

geography.quote: The Coastal Conservancy funds a wide variety of projects along the California coast, San Francisco Bay, and in coastal watersheds

access.quote: The first step in the application process is to submit a pre-application.

window.quote: Most Conservancy grants are awarded through a rolling pre-application solicitation.

amount.quote: it is anticipated that most grants will be between $200,000 and $5,000,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Grantee Required Match - No grantee match is required.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: Other community-based organizations and non-federally-recognized tribes may apply with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor

effort.quote: Applicants will first submit a pre-application.
If a preapplication meets the Conservancy's Eligibility Criteria and there is available Conservancy funding for the project, applicants will be invited to submit a full application.
Conservancy staff will evaluate applications based on the Project Selection Criteria.
Within 60 days, you will receive notification whether you are being asked to submit a full application or if your project is not eligible for Conservancy funding.
All grants must be approved by the Coastal Conservancy Board.

eligibility.quote: Consistent with purposes of the funding source.
Consistent with Conservancy enabling legislation: Public Resources Code, Division 21.

The grantee has the ability to administer the funds and conduct the project in a manner that will meet the State’s requirements and will protect the grantee from potential financial or legal risk. If the grantee does not have the capacity, they have partnered with a fiscal sponsor that will provide them the needed administrative support.
Site ownership/control - The grantee has or will have the legal right to carry out the project on the land on which the project is proposed.
The grantee has a plan for the long-term management, maintenance, and monitoring of the project.
Other community-based organizations and non-federally-recognized tribes may apply with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor
We do not fund operation and maintenance activities.

after_award.quote: Progress Reports Not Applicable Monthly or Quarterly throughout the contract term

documents.quote: Attach a map of the project location
